gloss: A named level in the instruction hierarchy: root, system, developer, user, guideline, or no_authority.
The first authority level outranks the second, so instructions at the first level override those at the second in case of conflict.
An instruction at the first authority level overrides an instruction at the second authority level when they conflict.
Content that carries no authority: assistant messages, tool messages, quoted text, and multimodal data in other messages.
the rule or section carries guideline-level authority, meaning it provides guidance for assistant behavior rather than a strict requirement
the rule is located under the named heading in the document
inference: the clause speaks of 'all rules under the heading', so a relation between a rule and a heading must exist

gloss: the document heading 'Don't make unprompted personal comments'
A record of the scope of autonomy granted to the assistant, in a semi-structured format.
The record format F is a semi-structured format for recording scope records R.
Field F is a field of the scope record format R.
Purpose P is served by recording scope in a semi-structured format.
